Theme

Body, health & movement · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

position noun

of the body

also posture, pose, stance, change position

classical

Cic. Off. 1.128: status incessus, sessiō accubitiō
Plaut. Mil. 206: crēbrō commūtat statūs

status, statūs m.

noun, fourth declension

posture, position of the body

How one holds the body, standing or at rest; Cicero sets beside it sessiō, the way of sitting, and accubitiō, of lying at table (Off. 1.128).

Examples

  • concrepuit digitīs: labōrat; crēbrō commūtat statūs

    he has snapped his fingers; he’s struggling; he keeps changing positionPlaut. Mil. 206

  • nūllum tormentum sentit supīna testūdō, inquiēta est tamen dēsīderiō nātūrālis statūs

    a tortoise on its back feels no pain, but it is restless, longing for its natural positionSen. Ep. 121.8

  • status incessus, sessiō accubitiō, vultus oculī manuum mōtus teneat illud decōrum

    let our posture and walk, our sitting and lying at table, our expression, our eyes and the movements of our hands keep to what is fittingCic. Off. 1.128

See also sit up straight!, position.
